correctness.rationale: Reconstructed detailed-balance stationary distribution and the fixed-group, fixed-prior weak-import limit. Exact arithmetic confirms the pooled finite-difference identity. The overshoot condition follows from a strictly increasing scalar bracket; the Lambert expression and log-log cutoff follow analytically. Geometric bounds make the rare-component error uniform over all observable integer counts, and the one-step phase comparison proves the sharp lattice maximum. The physically inoperative all-infected index is excluded. The extracted standard-library code performs finite diagnostics only, not infinite certification.

The assessed separate theorem gives the sharp integer threshold for exceeding the largest within-group marginal rate, the necessary and sufficient group-size cutoff, its log-log asymptotic, and a uniform maximal excess with nonconstant log-periodic leading coefficient. Checked primary main texts do not state these assertions; priority limits, especially unavailable 2023 supplementary material, remain explicit.

The known exact two-atom rate formula could be used to derive the new conclusion elsewhere; historical priority beyond checked accessible primary literature remains provisional.

value.rationale: The maximum underlying physical slope is the natural baseline for assessing whether an apparent pooled increment indicates within-group reinforcement. This theorem specifies exactly the first group size where that benchmark can fail, then shows an unbounded logarithmic false excess and integer-lattice modulation when a rare faster group becomes vanishingly rare. The exact cutoff and scaling are motivated observability invariants of the two-rate model, not arbitrary parameter instances or a restatement of qualitative Simpson bias.
